beats.care: If you order groceries in minutes, check expiry dates and seals on arrival. You can complain to FSSAI if something is off.
beats.what: Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration suspended licences of five warehouses run by Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer, Blinkit and Zomato Hyperpure.
beats.why: The FDA says expired, damaged or rejected food was sold on through middlemen instead of being destroyed, and found rats and cockroaches.

cards.body: Seven teams raided warehouses and disposal centres in Bhiwandi, Ambernath and Khed on 14 and 15 October, after tip-offs gathered from 23 September to 5 October. The seized stock was worth about ₹48 lakh. The companies' responses were not reported.
At its Pune-area warehouse, the FDA says the cold room was above 5°C, packets leaked, food sat on the floor and cockroaches were found.

cards.body: Hyperpure's invoices showed cheap sales to a Bengaluru 'disposal' buyer that investigators initially found did not appear to exist.
